newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LEICESTER TRY SWIPE-CARDS TO COMBAT TROUBLEMAKERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEICESTER TRY SWIPE-CARDS TO COMBAT TROUBLEMAKERS.

text.p: Leicester City chairman Tom Smeaton said on Monday his club are to experiment with a swipe-card entry system following crowd trouble at their F.A. Cup match with Chelsea on Sunday.
The club are to test the new hi-tech system before the end of the season and if it is successful Leicester will introduce it for all fans next season.
Ten fans were arrested at Filbert Street after Chelsea followers who had infiltrated the home end began fighting with Leicester supporters.
The fifth round match, which ended 2-2, was held up for five minutes as about 50 police and stewards fought to control about 100 troublemakers.
The incident was a throwback to the type of crowd trouble that blighted English football from the mid-1960s to the late 1980s, but it is rarely evident now.
The English F.A. has called for police reports into the trouble before deciding what action to take.
But looking to the future, Smeaton added: "The swipe card will contain a picture and allow fans to buy drinks and club merchandising in a similar way to a credit or debit card.
"I am very keen on security and also new technology. I think the idea of fans queueing in the rain to pay cash to get a ticket to get into a game is medieval.''
The card will also make it easier for the club to identify troublemakers and ban them. The date for a trial of the card has yet to be decided.
Smeaton said Chelsea fans managed to purchase tickets in areas used by home fans with the help of compliant taxi drivers from Leicester.
He said: Taxi drivers had been given money by Chelsea fans and kept turning up and buying tickets. As soon as we realised what was happening we stopped selling them tickets.''
The match will be replayed at Stamford Bridge on February 26.
